main_issue: Whether Agent D may keep wearing her cross tucked in or taped under her clothes tomorrow, or must take it off entirely to comply with the no-visible-jewellery rule.

A-B.evidence: A (T3) says rule applies to everyone, D must remove; B (T2, T4) pushes same; at T24-25 A says taping isn't the same as taking it off and B replies 'Right. It has to be the same for everyone.'

A-C.evidence: C (T13) says A should just check it in the morning; A (T15) refuses; C (T20, T22) says taping works and it's settled; A (T24) says 'It's not settled' and that the cross must come off.

A-D.evidence: D offers to tuck it in (T6, T8) and tape it (T16); A rejects each offer (T7, T9, T15) and at T24 insists the only sure way is to not wear it.

B-C.evidence: B insists D must remove it like B's earrings (T10, T12, T21); C says it's different, 'It's settled. Let it go' (T11, T22).

B-D.evidence: B says tucking and taping is still wearing it (T10, T17); D replies 'You can't wear earrings under a shirt' (T18); no shift by T25.

C-D.evidence: C backs tucking and a morning check (T13), D agrees (T14); C says 'Taping it works' (T20) in line with D's offer (T16).
